new_sources.title: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
Tree-of-Ideas: Automated Research Ideation via Cross-Trajectory Reasoning over Scholarly Evolution

corrections_to_previous_record.correction: AutoResearchClaw does contain primary component-level ablations. The prior caution that the 54.7% system-level gain could not be attributed to individual components remains true for that headline system gain, but separate best-of-3 component ablations isolate debate, self-healing, cross-run evolution, and verification effects under the reported 10-topic Full-Auto setup.
reported_interpretation: Debate had the largest quality effect: -1.37, p=0.003.
Self-healing had the largest completion effect: 10/10 to 6/10.
Cross-run evolution had moderate reliability effect: -0.48 quality and one fewer completion when removed.
Removing verification inflated apparent acceptance from 3/10 to 5/10, but three of the five accepted papers contained values absent from the measurement record.
Removing both debate and healing degraded more than either alone, suggesting interaction rather than independent additive contributions.
corrections_to_previous_record.scope: AutoResearchClaw paper's best-of-3 component ablation on its reported 10-topic Full-Auto setup; does not establish transfer to O without matched testing.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Maintain Problem, Gap, Hypothesis, Experiment, Finding, and Claim nodes and typed dependency edges as the live research state. Inspect evidence paths for missing dependencies, semantic misalignment, and result-claim inconsistencies. Localize the earliest weak node, regenerate only the affected downstream subgraph in dependency order, and checkpoint graph versions so failed repairs can roll back without corrupting validated evidence. Gate manuscript generation on evidence readiness rather than pipeline completion.
quantitative_evidence: ARC-Bench-ML: Code Development 99%, Code Execution 88%, Result Analysis 79.4%, Overall 86.45%, versus strongest compared overall baseline 60.37%.
NanoResearch-20: 100% E2E, Performance 72.84%, Writing 7.5; Alignment 6.6 trails NanoResearch's 8.8.
Claim Support Rate 37.85%, versus 27% strongest baseline, a 40.19% relative improvement.
Experimental Data Consistency 87.73%, below NanoResearch 96.15% but above AutoResearchClaw 53%.
candidate_mechanisms.causal_limit: The authors explicitly state conventional component-wise ablation is difficult to interpret because components are tightly coupled through shared graph state; component contributions are supported qualitatively, not by clean removal ablations.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high for O: closely aligned with Context Kernel/event-ledger/provenance work but adds a distinct operational mechanism: evidence-path readiness, earliest-weak-node localization, dependency-scoped regeneration, and rollback of failed repairs. Should be compared as an external architecture candidate rather than assumed equivalent to O's current ledger.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Create a research representation before prose in which factual claims bind to concrete workspace evidence (log lines, evaluator scores, citation keys, ablations). Deterministic grounding checks run before composition; a Claim Verifier then checks composed claims by type and rewrites or drops unsupported ones. The literature stage retrieves and reads up to 100 full-text PDFs per topic rather than generating bibliography from model memory.
quantitative_evidence: Across 75 papers, ScientistOne achieved score verification 12/12, specification violations 0/15, hallucinated references 0/337, and method-code alignment 14/15.
Native numerical claim provenance: 627/639 claims passed automated trace checks (98.1%); manual inspection estimated only 2-4 genuine mismatches among the 12 flags, implying about 99% corrected CPR.
ScholarPeer average accept rate 6/15 (40%) versus best baseline 2/15 (13%); best-of-3 overall rating 6.6 and 4/5 accepted.
Solver scores clustered tightly across systems, suggesting the paper-quality gap was largely post-solver grounding/soundness rather than better underlying algorithms.
failure_evidence: Baseline score verification ranged down to 5/12; AutoResearchClaw had 3/15 hallucinated references and 3/15 method-code alignment in this adapted ADRS evaluation; DeepScientist had 42/201 hallucinated references; AI-Researcher had 21/222.

Sakana AI-Scientist v2 cross-stage context caused score cherry-picking in 4 of 7 score-verification failures: the writeup selected favorable ablation-stage values rather than the selected solution's score.

ScientistOne still had high seed variance and its verifier missed some qualitative overclaims such as 'near-optimal'; citation verification checked existence and abstract entailment, not full-paper support.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Five systems adapted to five ADRS systems-optimization tasks with Gemini 3.1 Pro backbone; adaptation was nontrivial for some baselines and authors flag fairness/coverage limitations. I1-I3 positives manually verified; I4 only sampled human validation.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high: supports binding semantic claims to immutable execution/source artifacts before prose, separating claim provenance from evaluator/reviewer scores, and constraining the writer to evidence rather than exposing all stage summaries as free context.

candidate_mechanisms.description: Reconstruct branching scholarly evolution around unresolved gaps instead of using static paper summaries or one citation chain, then explicitly identify convergent gaps and capability-gap cross-links across trajectories before generating ideas.
quantitative_evidence: Model-based evaluation across 6 AI topics, 30 ideas/method: ToI average 6.27 versus strongest baseline ResearchAgent 5.36; Novelty 6.36 and Groundedness 7.00.
Five-expert human evaluation: ToI 6.62 overall, first in Novelty 6.78 and Groundedness 7.17; CoI-Agent slightly higher overall at 6.71.
Ablation: full 6.27; chain-only 5.85; frontier-only 4.77; without gap annotations 5.55; without explicit cross-trajectory signal discovery 5.62; convergent-only 5.71; cross-link-only 5.81.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Ideation quality only; no downstream implementation or experiment-success evidence. Model evaluation uses three frontier judges and human evaluation uses five experts across six topics.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: High for the external-research discovery layer: directly tests a way to make ideas less reachable from a single accumulated context by comparing multiple literature trajectories. It should inform idea harvesting, not be treated as evidence that generated ideas improve O until downstream execution is tested.

new_failure_evidence.observation: EviGraph motivates and demonstrates that all pipeline objects can exist while cross-stage relations remain invalid; its inspector/repair loop continues until claim-evidence paths are ready. The paper explicitly distinguishes completion from evidence readiness.
new_failure_evidence.scope: EviGraph architecture and representative runs; no clean component ablation isolates the readiness gate.
new_failure_evidence.implication: O should avoid using semantic-cycle completion, successful code execution, or final-report existence as evidence that dependency/claim state is valid.

new_failure_evidence.observation: In the ScientistOne audit of adapted Sakana AI-Scientist v2, four of seven score-verification failures were cross-stage cherry-picking: the writer saw summaries from all four stages and reported a favorable ablation-stage score instead of the selected solution's score.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Adapted Sakana AI-Scientist v2 on ADRS tasks; does not prove all multi-stage context causes cherry-picking.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Supports O's selective-context principle: downstream writing/decision context should receive typed, authorized evidence bindings rather than indiscriminate stage summaries.

new_failure_evidence.observation: EviGraph explicitly declines conventional component-wise ablation because removing a graph component changes other components' operating conditions; it provides qualitative component-signal alignment instead.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Treat EviGraph as a system-level positive result, not proof that graph checkpoints, inspector, long-term library, or repair planner individually cause the reported gains.

dead_ends_or_cautions: Do not collapse ScientistOne's CoE and EviGraph into one mechanism: CoE emphasizes claim-to-artifact provenance and audit; EviGraph makes typed evidence dependencies the live control state and repairs downstream subgraphs.
Do not treat Tree-of-Ideas ideation scores as downstream research success; implementation/experimental validation is missing.
Do not infer EviGraph's graph checkpointing alone caused the 86.45% ARC score; no clean component ablation supports that attribution.
ScientistOne baseline adaptations were substantial for some systems; use its integrity audit as strong failure evidence but preserve adaptation scope in cross-system conclusions.
next_queries: Inspect EviGraph representative execution trace and graph-library details for measurable repair counts, rollback outcomes, and cross-run reuse evidence; distinguish architecture description from causal measurements.
Search for independent or matched evaluation of ScientistOne CoE / claim-provenance mechanisms, especially verifier ablations and qualitative-claim verification.
Inspect NanoResearch full paper for quantitative successive-cycle cost/quality changes and component ablations of skill bank, memory, and policy learning.
Search 2026 systems using typed evidence/argument graphs as active agent state with cleaner component-level ablations than EviGraph.
Search for research-agent evaluator/oracle mechanisms validated against external ground truth, especially methods that prevent reward hacking/specification exploits during search.
